Petitioners/Accused No.2 And 3.
 These Petitions, Coming On For Order

S, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR  ORAL ORDER 1.

The petitioners in these petitions are sought to be prosecuted for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2. The prosecution alleges that accused No.1 is the husband and accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in-law of the de facto complainant.
It is alleged that they subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and demanded dowry from her parental home.
3. The parties are present before this Court and have filed an application for compounding, stating that they have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves.
As per the terms of the settlement:
Accused No.1 and the de facto complainant have agreed to dissolve their marriage mutually.

3 NC: 2025:KHC-D:2371
Accused No.1 has agreed to pay a sum of  30 lakhs towards permanent alimony to the de facto complainant.
The application is placed on record.
Accused No.1, who is present before the Court, has handed over  15 lakhs to the de facto complainant, who has acknowledged receipt of the same.
Accused No.1 has agreed to pay the balance amount of  15 lakhs immediately upon the mutual dissolution of their marriage.
The de facto complainant has agreed to withdraw all allegations against the petitioners and has no objection to quashing the impugned proceedings.

The gold ornaments have been returned to the de facto complainant, and she has acknowledged receipt of the same.
4.

Although the offences alleged are cognizable and non- compoundable, considering the fact that the parties have amicably resolved their dispute, subjecting the petitioners to trial would be a futile exercise.
Given the remote and bleak probability of conviction, in light of the settlement, the continuation of criminal proceedings would amount to an abuse of the process of law.
5. Accordingly, the petitions are allowed.
The impugned proceedings in C.C. No. 443/2024, pending before the IV Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Ballari, are hereby quashed.
